subject: ventures/card-processing-fee-audit
professional: a merchant-services / payments consultant who reviews small-merchant processing statements for a living; first checks: does the pass-through estimate respect Regulation II regulated-debit pricing and the per-item interchange that dominates small tickets, are assessments and network fees (Visa APF/FANF, Mastercard NABU) right and classified as pass-through, is markup derived in the right direction, can a flat-rate quote (Stripe/Square) be compared, and does the tool ever tell a merchant there is no markup when there is

evidence.correctness: Ran auditStatement (node scratchpad/cpfa.mjs). The worked example recomputes by hand: effective rate 1300/42000 = 3.0952%; mid blend 0.85x1.65%+0.15x2.15% = 1.725%, interchange 724.50+140 = 864.50, assessments 58.80+28 = 86.80, pass-through 951.30 (low 867.30, high 1059.45), markup 348.70 (240.55-432.70), quote 951.30+105+140+10 = 1206.30, $1,124.40/yr: all match the tool and the page. A Helcim in-person quote (0.40% + $0.08, $0 monthly) priced by hand 951.30+168+112 = 1231.30 matches. But the band is not anchored to the network rules it claims to estimate. (1) A debit-heavy grocer: 1,000 x $40, 100% card present, all regulated debit. Regulation II (12 CFR 235.3(b) 21c + 0.05%, 235.4 +1c fraud adjustment) gives $0.24 interchange per item = $240; Visa debit assessments 0.13% + ~$0.0155 = $67.50; with a real IC+0.30%+$0.10+$25 markup of $245 the bill is $552.50 (1.38%). The tool's LOWEST pass-through is $756, so it reports markup $0-$0 and the headline says 'this model cannot identify processor markup in it' while 44% of the bill is markup. (2) A $5-ticket cafe, 60% regulated debit / 40% consumer credit at Visa CPS Retail 1.51%+$0.10: true interchange $1,629.60 on $40,000 (4.07%) vs the tool's HIGH interchange $1,560, so even the 'most flattering' markup reading overstates markup. The arithmetic is right; the pass-through it subtracts can be wrong by more than the band on common merchant types, and the headline output then is wrong. 2.
evidence.completeness: Every README feature works end to end: effective rate, average fee per transaction, pass-through band, markup band in $ and % of sales, re-priced IC+ quote, 2-4 shape notes (fixed fees, small/large ticket, keyed share, quote win/lose), save/restore/reset in localStorage, usage opt-out honouring DNT/GPC (usage.mjs:39), error path clears stale figures (page.test.mjs:8). Three content pages present and linked; sitemap covers all pages; served-copy reports no placeholder origin. Partial: the Helcim page tells users to enter Helcim's in-person AND online rates as the quote, but the quote has one markup and one per-item field (no card-present/not-present split); the guide says to 'price your own statement both ways' (flat vs IC+) but the tool cannot price a flat-rate quote. No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: node --test *.test.mjs in the venture: 49 pass, 0 fail (0.49 s). Five seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: CNP per-item interchange x1.5 caught; quote markup /1000 caught; large-ticket threshold 150->250 caught; keyed-share threshold 50->15 caught; at-or-below-pass-through threshold high.total -> mid.total SURVIVED (the headline-message branch boundary is untested between mid and high). 4 of 5 caught. All expected values are the author's own RATE_MODEL arithmetic; no test checks the model against a regulated-debit or published interchange case, so the domain defect above cannot be caught by the suite.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (293 lines), index.html script (210-280), usage.mjs, all tests. Clean single engine, passThroughAt shared by low/mid/high, every input range-checked with a specific message, textContent only, error path clears figures. Defects: interchange per-item uses RATE_MODEL.cardPresent.perTransaction for all volume (calc.mjs:79), so the cardNotPresent.perTransaction constant is dead and a future edit to it silently does nothing; the comment at calc.mjs:172 says 'even the cheapest reading of the networks' share' for a test against high.total, the most expensive reading, and the FAQ copies the inversion; README test count stale.
evidence.claims: Checked 9 claims. Backed: disclaimer and no-warranty on all four pages (page.test.mjs:43); no network request (grep finds no fetch/sendBeacon/XHR in shipped files); DNT/GPC honoured (usage.mjs:39); worked-example figures $951.30 / $348.70 / $240.55-$432.70 (recomputed); café vs contractor table +1.00% / +0.05% (420/42000, 21/42000); Stripe 2.9% + $0.30 dated and sourced. Not backed or wrong: FAQ 'whole bill is explained by the cheapest reading of network pass-through' (index.html:144) describes the opposite of the code (fees <= high.total); 'Are the fixed monthly fees really markup? In substance, yes' (index.html:136, calc.mjs:241) ignores network fixed fees such as Visa's Fixed Acquirer Network Fee, which is pass-through; Helcim page 'enter those as the competing quote's markup fields' (vs-helcim-rate-calculator.html:87) for two rate pairs the form cannot hold; 'flat-rate ... usually [more expensive], and the gap grows with volume' (what-is-a-good-effective-rate-for-card-processing.html:88) uncited; RATE_MODEL 'typical published ranges' cites no schedule or edition (calc.mjs:26-34); README '29 assertions' vs 49 tests (README.md:72); Helcim and Stripe rates could not be re-fetched (proxy 403) and match the auditor's knowledge of those pages.
evidence.fitness: Walked a small merchant's job: read five numbers off a statement, get a split, compare a quote. For a credit-heavy card-present retailer with a $20-$150 ticket it produces a usable, honestly-banded figure and a dollar comparison. It fails the job for the merchants most likely to be on bad pricing: debit-heavy grocery/gas/QSR (told no markup exists), micro-ticket cafes (markup overstated), merchants offered a flat-rate quote (Stripe/Square cannot be entered as the comparison), and mixed CP/online merchants comparing a vendor that prices the two differently. A payments consultant would still need the statement's interchange-category detail; the tool does not ask for debit share, which is the single input that moves the band most.
evidence.domain: Compared against Regulation II (12 CFR 235.3/235.4: 21c + 0.05% + 1c for regulated debit), Visa/Mastercard published interchange structure (CPS Retail credit about 1.51%+$0.10, exempt debit about 0.80%+$0.15, CNP and rewards tiers 1.8%-2.5%+$0.10, commercial higher) and network assessments (Visa 0.14% credit / 0.13% debit plus APF per item, Mastercard 0.13%-0.14% plus NABU; FANF monthly). Assessments and the CP/CNP credit bands are plausible; markup inversion (high pass-through -> low markup) is correct. Departures: no debit/credit split, so regulated debit (often a third to a half of card-present volume) is priced like credit and the 'low' end is not a floor; per-item interchange fixed at $0.10 regardless of card type; no commercial, Amex or downgrade/non-qualified modelling; network fixed fees classed as markup. A consultant would not sign off on the band as a floor/ceiling.

defects.what: Pass-through model has no debit/credit split and ignores Regulation II (21c + 0.05% + 1c), so the 'low' band is not a floor. A debit-heavy merchant (1,000 x $40, all regulated debit, true markup $245 of a $552.50 bill) is told markup is $0-$0 and 'this model cannot identify processor markup'; a $5-ticket cafe's true interchange ($1,629.60) sits above the band's top ($1,560), overstating markup

Per-item interchange is a flat $0.10 for every card (and always read from cardPresent.perTransaction, making cardNotPresent.perTransaction dead); regulated debit is $0.22, exempt debit about $0.15, so small-ticket pass-through is understated
Helcim page tells users to enter Helcim's in-person (0.40%+8c) and online (0.50%+25c) rates as the quote, but the form has a single markup and per-item field with no card-present/not-present split
No way to compare a flat-rate quote (Stripe/Square style), though the guide tells merchants to 'price your own statement both ways'
All flat monthly fees are called markup ('In substance, yes'), but network fixed fees such as Visa's Fixed Acquirer Network Fee are pass-through; the tool subtracts nothing for them

FAQ and code comment say the at-or-below test uses the 'cheapest reading' of pass-through; the code tests against high.total, the most expensive reading. When fees fall between mid and high, the headline says no markup can be identified while the metric shows a positive mid markup; the boundary is untested (mutant survived)
RATE_MODEL bands cite no schedule, edition or date ('typical published ranges')
'Is flat-rate more expensive? Usually, and the gap grows with volume' has no source or worked number
README says '29 assertions'; the suite runs 49 tests

verdict: A clean, well-tested, privacy-respecting five-number statement splitter whose arithmetic is right: the worked example (3.10%, pass-through $951.30 in $867.30-$1,059.45, markup $348.70 in $240.55-$432.70, quote $1,206.30) and a Helcim in-person re-pricing recompute by hand, and 4 of 5 seeded bugs are caught. But the pass-through band it subtracts is not anchored to the network rules: with no debit/credit split and no Regulation II pricing, a debit-heavy merchant with $245 of real markup on a $552.50 bill is told there is no identifiable markup, and a $5-ticket cafe's true interchange sits above the band's top. Claims slip in places (inverted 'cheapest reading' FAQ, Helcim two-rate instruction the form cannot hold, network fixed fees called markup). Correctness and claims are 2, so it does not meet the bar; completeness is 3, so it is finished.
